exposure: Maternal baseline hemoglobin concentration (≤109, 110-119, 120-129, and ≥130 g/L)
cohort: Two cohorts of infants from China: Cohort 1 (n=17,423) born during 2006-2009 in northeastern China and Cohort 2 (n=122,777) born during 1993-1996 in southeastern China
finding: Cesarean delivery was not associated with anemia at 6 months but was associated with an increased risk of anemia at 12 and 58 months of age, regardless of maternal hemoglobin levels or cesarean delivery subtypes.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was found to be associated with an increased risk of anemia in children at 12 and 58 months of age, suggesting a possible link between mode of delivery and later iron status.
